Water Supply Conditions Update
items.text: Water Supply Conditions Update In response to a question as to how bad water conditions are and what is being doing about it, Steve Ritchie, Assistant General Manager (AGM) Water, indicted that there is no way to know if it will get better or worse. He stated there is a decent amount of storage on the San Joaquin side which is in better shape than the Sacramento side. He stated in early July customers were asked to try to comply with the Governor’s call for 15% voluntary reduction from 2020 levels, noting that a 10% reduction level has been achieved. He stated that even with the reduction, if dry conditions continue that this fall, there will be a call for more reductions beginning in January. He noted that additional water has been added down the river this summer to supplement required flows

Update on SFPUC Operations During COVID-19 Emergency
items.text: Update on SFPUC Operations During COVID-19 Emergency Michael Carlin, Acting GM, stated that due to 50% of the SFPUC workforce - the field crews who currently work on-site, combined with the 50% of the workforce who work remotely, there has been no disruption of core services throughout the pandemic. He thanked everyone for their work. He discussed growing concerns by the City with the Delta variant. He stated that all employees are required to mask while indoors. He indicated that employees are required to report their vaccination status by August 12th and that currently 90% of employees have reported their status with 100% reporting expected soon. He stated City employees will be required to be vaccinated within 10 weeks of the FDA’s approval of the vaccine. He noted as a condition of hiring, future City employees will be required to show proof of vaccination. He indicated mobile pop-up vaccination sites have been made available at SFPUC sites. Acting GM Carlin stated that the City’s Department of Human Resources is planning to require employees to report to work at least two days per week beginning in September and that the Telecommute Policy is being revised. Scheduling of return- to-work will begin in a phased approach, which he briefly discussed. items.title: Tunnel Engineering Services for the Folsom Area Stormwater Improvement Project with McMillen Jacobs Associates/Stantec
items.text: Approve Amendment No. 3 to Agreement No. PRO.0101, Tunnel Engineering Services for the Folsom Area Stormwater Improvement Project with McMillen Jacobs Associates/Stantec, Joint Venture; and authorize the General Manager to execute Amendment No. 3, extending the agreement duration by 19 months, for a total agreement duration of 55 months, with no change to the agreement amount. Derek Adams, Project Manager, began with review of the project’s background (upstream components – 12,500 linear feet) and status, indicating that planning is complete, the design phase is in progress, environmental clearing is pending, and right-of-way acquisition is on-going. He reviewed Folsom Project contracts (1) Initial Pipe Contract $7,300,000, (2) Sewer Pipe Contract $67,200,000, (3) Large Pipe Contract $19,000,000, and (4) Tunnel/Shaft Contract $97,000,000. He reviewed the design and construction schedule, total project cost estimate ($290,977,475), and design challenges. Mr. Adams reviewed reasons for the requested extension and discussed next steps. Commissioner Ajami expressed frustration with the situation with Caltrans, the pile foundations, and that the issues weren’t discussed earlier. Mr. Adams addressed the situation and the options that had been discussed. He stated that he was not aware of due diligence efforts related to the project as that was before his work on the project began.
